entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Nilesh Jagtap, learned Govt. Advocate for  respondent/State.
Let the record of the court below be requisitioned.
Heard on I.A.No.7502/2019, which is an application for suspension of sentence pending the revision.

The applicant has been convicted for offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced for 6 months' R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/-, failing which sentence of 1 month's R.I. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that short sentence has been awarded to the applicant and the applicant will suffer if the sentence is not suspended at this stage.
Counsel for the State has opposed the application for suspension of sentence.
Considering the submissions made by the counsel for the applicant, the period of sentence, nature of the case and the fact that this revision is not likely to be heard and disposed off at an early date

, it is directed that on deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (fifty thousand rupees) with separate surety bond in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 25.11.2019 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry, the applicant/accused be released on bail and the substantive sentence under revision shall remain suspended.
IA No.7502/2019 is accordingly disposed off.

(Ms. Vandana Kasrekar) Judge Abhay Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr. Sanjeev ... on 11 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57872493/
